Robotics and Autonomous SystemsAuthor keywordsquadruped navigationreach-avoid controlsafe robot learningEasyChair keyphraseshigh level (150), frozen tracker (110), reach avoid (95), minimum cost reach (95), robotics science and systems (80), goal reaching (76), unsafe set (70), high level learning (63), jointly with sr (63), collision free goal reaching (60), budget selection (60), pretrained frozen velocity tracker (60), balance gait coordination and action smoothness (51), cumulative cost (50), cost margin (50), reach avoid control (47), body velocity commands (47), cost m camra (47), high level velocity (47), learning and deployment (47), frozen velocity interface (47), high level learning and budget (46), learning and initial budget selection (46), maximum planar distance between time (46), minimum cost (40), hierarchical control (40), success rate (40), neural information processing systems (40), physical robot (40), institute of software chinese (40), budget violation (40), navigation learning (40), budget accounting (40), cc paper files paper (40), quadruped navigation (40), goal reaching obstacle avoidance (40), paired nominal (40), both margins (40), nominal executed (40), interpreted jointly (40), low cost route selection (40), policy and margins fixed (40), cost and geometric margins (40), learning and budget selection (40), route selection among multiple (40), collision and budget violation (40), high level navigation learning (40), quadruped closed loop execution (40), moderately cluttered narrow passage (40)AbstractThe deployment of minimum-cost reach-avoid control on a physical quadruped robot is investigated. The challenges of coupled locomotion-navigation learning and model-execution mismatch are addressed through hierarchical control and two data-calibrated margins. Locomotion stabilization is separated from high-level navigation learning by a pretrained, frozen velocity tracker. Before high-level learning, nominal budget accounting is corrected by the cost margin, and the unsafe set is expanded by the geometric margin. Across three navigation scenarios, a success rate of 73.3% and a budget violation rate of 9.0% are obtained with the resulting calibrated minimum-cost reach-avoid (CaMRA) system, compared with 70.7% and 14.0% for uncalibrated RC-PPO. The distinct roles and deployment limits of these corrections are examined through ablation, held-out calibration, and physical-robot studies.
